message: architect.completeness-critic.finding (medium): Manifest has no acceptance criteria block. The PLAN's brain constraint explicitly requires 'Given-When-Then with runnable assertions — not prose. Each AC must name the fixture file and expected exit code so it can be independently verified.' The manifest instead has delivery bullets that describe what to build. Delivery item 3 is circular: 'covers every case listed in the acceptance criteria with fixture files' — those criteria are not listed anywhere in the manifest. Without named fixtures and expected exit codes, a developer can write happy-path-only tests or unit tests that never invoke the function through main(), satisfying python -m pytest tests/ while the lint is never actually wired into the script's call chain. The suppression-env-fakes-the-pass brain constraint (must exercise BOTH error path exit 1 and happy path exit 0) is stated in the PLAN but propagated to the manifest only as prose intent, not as a verifiable criterion.

message: architect.completeness-critic.finding (medium): The manifest's coupled-changes item 3 says the new test file 'covers all ACs below', but no Acceptance Criteria section appears anywhere in the manifest. The PLAN explicitly cites the brain constraint spec-driven-work-items — 'Each AC must name the fixture file and expected exit code so it can be independently verified' — yet the manifest delivers zero Given-When-Then assertions. The suppression-env-fakes-the-pass antipattern (also cited in the PLAN) requires explicit ACs for both the error path (unknown slug → FAIL, exit 1) and the happy path (valid slug → OK, exit 0); without them, the PM has no runnable target and the vacuous-gate risk the PLAN flagged under edge case 6 remains open in the manifest itself.
